title: Hidden Gems
intro: Locally-known spots beyond tourist traps. September timing favorable (fewer tourists than peak summer). Lesser-known sites doubly valuable for crowd avoidance. Deepens shopping, food, and nature interests with authentic local experiences.

tables.caption: Beijing — 5 Places Locals Love
rows: Wudaoying Hutong
Sat/Sun morning 9:30 AM — hip hutong parallel to Nanluoguxiang; coffee, vintage, craft beer
798 Art Zone
Weekday afternoon (galleries closed Mon) — former factory district; Asia's best urban art space; 30 min taxi
Sanlitun Soho Rooftop
5:30–7 PM golden hour — unmarked terrace; sunset over eastern skyline
Ghost Street (Guijie)
11 PM–2 AM — 150+ 24hr restaurants; fried crayfish and hotpot; 10 min DiDi from Dongcheng
Coal Hill (Jingshan) North View
5:30–6:30 PM Sept — sunset glow on Forbidden City rooftops; far fewer people than midday

tables.caption: Hanoi — 5 Places Locals Love
rows: Tay Ho West Lake Circuit
6–8 AM dawn — 17 km lakeside path; bicycle ~50,000 VND/day; temple islands
Long Bien Bridge at Dawn
5–7 AM — 1902 French-colonial iron bridge; local vendors; train crosses twice daily
Pho Thin Bo Ho (13 Lò Đúc)
6–9 AM only; arrive by 7:30 — 60-year recipe; locals' pho, no tourists
Dong Tac Market
7–9 AM peak — neighborhood wet market; fresh flowers, live fish; no tourist pricing
Nhan My Bakery
From 6 AM — best bánh mì locals keep secret; ask hotel or "Bánh mì ngon nhất gần đây?"

tables.caption: Hội An / Đà Nẵng — 5 Places Locals Love
rows: An Bang Beach
Morning Sept weekdays — locals' beach vs tourist Cua Dai; bicycle ~15 min from Old Town
Kim Bong Carpentry Village
8–11 AM workshops active — basket boat from dock ~30,000 VND; centuries-old woodworking
Tra Que Vegetable Village
7–10 AM before heat — organic farm 3 km away; farm-to-table ~$20/person
Thanh Ha Pottery Village
Bicycle ~20 min — 400+ year foot-operated wheels; wheel-throwing experience
Non Nước Stone Carving Village
Between Marble Mountains and Đà Nẵng — 500+ workshops; buy direct from artisans

bullets.heading: "Only Here" Experiences
items: Beijing: Peking Opera masks painted to order in Liulichang; siheyuan courtyard breakfast in 600-year-old hutong
Hanoi: Bia Hoi Corner — fresh beer 5,000–10,000 VND at plastic stools; Water Puppet Theatre (11th-century art form)
Hội An: Floating flower candles on Thu Bon River at dusk (~10,000 VND); Cao Lầu noodles from Cham well water — unique to this town

bullets.heading: Neighborhood Deep-Dives
items: Beijing: Beixinqiao — young Beijingers live/eat here; zero tourist infrastructure; century-old teahouse
Hanoi: Tay Ho (West Lake) — expat area, Tran Quoc Pagoda on island, far fewer tourists than Old Quarter

bullets.heading: Nighttime Secrets
items: Beijing: Drum/Bell Tower squares after 10 PM — guitars, snacks, conversation under ancient towers
Hanoi: Nha Tho Street (Cathedral) — wine bars, boutique shops; 7–10 PM Parisian vibe
Hội An: Ancient Town lantern light after 7 PM; Full Moon Festival turns off electricity (confirm lunar calendar)

bullets.heading: Cross-Border Connections
items: Confucian traditions in both — ancestor shrines in homes; ask and locals light up
Chinese immigrants brought Won Ton → evolved into Cao Lầu; Phung Kien Assembly Hall is pure Southern Chinese temple style
Bánh mì (French-Vietnamese fusion) parallels Beijing duck and Vietnamese thịt heo quay — shared Cantonese roasting roots

callouts.text: 798 Art Zone: add to Day 4 afternoon if shopping energy is low
Non Nước Village: large pieces shippable internationally; small pieces (under $50) perfect carry-home buys
5 hidden gems per location; 2 "only here" experiences each; all explicitly lower-crowd alternatives
